title: Local device functions don't correctly restore previously active graphics device
description:
This is a follow-up on #138, #245, and #267 

The local device functions like `local_pdf()` don't correctly restore the previous open graphics device but instead restores the highest-numbered device.

## reprex

```r
library(grDevices)
pdf(NULL); pdf(NULL)   # devices 2 and 3 open
dev.set(2L)            # make device 2 active
dev.cur()
#> pdf
#>   2

f <- function() withr::local_pdf(NULL)   # opens device 4, closes it on exit
f()
dev.cur()
#> pdf
#>   3                  # expected 2

graphics.off()
```

## the fix

The old active device has to be recorded *before* the device function opens the new one, because
`defer_dev_close()` can't recover it on its own.

```r
# Open a device with `open(new, ...)`, close it when `.local_envir` exits and
# then restore whichever device was active beforehand.
local_device <- function(open, new, ..., .local_envir = parent.frame()) {
  old <- grDevices::dev.cur()
  open(new, ...)
  defer_dev_close(old, .local_envir)
}

defer_dev_close <- function(old, frame) {
  cur <- grDevices::dev.cur()
  defer(dev_close(cur, old), envir = frame)
  # Note that unlike typical `local_` functions we return the current device
  # rather than the old one
  invisible(cur)
}

dev_close <- function(which, old) {
  # the user may have already closed the device inside the local scope
  if (which %in% grDevices::dev.list()) {
    grDevices::dev.off(which)
  }
  # `old` is the null device (1) if nothing was open beforehand (nothing to
  # restore) and may itself have been closed inside the local scope
  if (old != 1L && old %in% grDevices::dev.list()) {
    grDevices::dev.set(old)
  }
  invisible(old)
}
```

A PR that fixes this would currently create a merge conflict with PR #293 that also wants to edit every local device function so it may be desirable to accept or reject that PR first before fixing this.

title: [Feature request] `with_palette` to change the color palette
description:
`grDevices::palette` is a function that allows changing the color for plotting, for example,

```r
plot(1:10, col = 1)
```

renders the dots in black. However, 

```r
oldpal <- palette(c("orange", "black")); 
on.exit({palette(oldpal)})
plot(1:10, col = 1)
```

will render the plots in orange.

Imagine `plot(1:10, col = 1)` is the user's code, then without hard-coding the colors, you can change the colors with `palette()` calls.

title: Problem with local_seed?
description:
My understanding of 'local_seed' is that allows control of .Random.seed within a function, but restores the original .Random.seed on function exit.  (So that the RNG stream of the function _caller_ is not affected by random number generation _within_ the function.)  But that does not appear to happen (using withr version 3.0.2 with R 4.5.3).

```{r}
f1 <- function(n, seed) {
  withr::local_seed(seed)
  rnorm(n)
}

set.seed(42)
rslt1 <- rnorm(5)
seed1 <- .Random.seed
rslt2 <- f1(5, 42)
identical(rslt1, rslt2)  # TRUE, as expected
identical(seed1, .Random.seed)  # Also TRUE, as expected

# But using a different seed within f1 leaves .Random.seed changed even after return:
set.seed(42)
seed3 <- .Random.seed
rslt3 <- f1(5, 41)
identical(seed3, .Random.seed)  # FALSE
```

Apologies if I have misunderstood the purpose of local_seed, or if I'm not using it correctly.  Pointers to a more appropriate forum for this question are welcome.

title: Should `with_file()` restore overwritten files ?
description:
Like `rlang::with_bindings()` retores the original bindings if present.

At the moment it removes the file if it exists. That's not what I expected and I don't think it's ever useful.

``` r
file.create("foo.bar")
#> [1] TRUE
file.exists("foo.bar")
#> [1] TRUE
withr::with_file("foo.bar", NULL)
file.exists("foo.bar")
#> [1] FALSE
```

<sup>Created on 2025-04-09 with [reprex v2.1.0](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

I see also that the doc and code are inconsistent regarding the return value. The doc says it returns the output of the code, which makes a lot of sense to me, but the code returns the file invisibly.

title: Should the parameter `tmpdir` be superseded by a new `tempdir` parameter?
description:
If you look at the signature for `{withr}` functions that work with temporary directories and files,

```r
with_tempdir(
  code,
  clean = TRUE,
  pattern = "file",
  tmpdir = tempdir(),
  fileext = ""
)
```

title: Add short vignette on writing your own withr-like functions
description:
I think this technique is known to some, but not to many others and I can't find an existing demo within withr's docs (I could be wrong). But if I'm right, I think this would make a great short vignette.

Basically showing how to capture and pass along the environment that you want to schedule future actions on.

``` r
local_change_digits <- function(new_digits, envir = rlang::caller_env()) {
  op <- options(digits = new_digits)
  withr::defer(options(op), envir = envir)
}

fun <- function() {
  print("inside fun, before calling local_change_digits(): ")
  print(pi)
  
  local_change_digits(2)
```

title: How to undo call to `local_dir()` or `local_options()` in global environment?
description:
Hi,

I am wondering if it is possible to "undo" a call to any `withr::local_*()`, like `local_dir()` or `local_options()` when being run from the global environment (e.g. in a development/debugging scenario) and not from within a function or any well delimited code chunk?

If not, it would be a great feature.

Here is my problem, I am using `withr::local_dir()` in a `testthat` test to run a test in a local temp directory. Here is a small toy example:
```R
# R/fun.R
my_fun <- function() {
    a <- 10
    save("a", file = "data.RData") # my function create a dummy file
}
```
```R
# tests/testthat/test-fun.R
test_that("my_fun", {
    test_dir <- withr::local_tempdir()
    withr::local_dir(test_dir) # I move to the temp dir to run the test
    my_fun()
    expect_true(file.exists("data.RData")) # I check that the file is indeed created
})
```

When I am doing some development/debugging, it may happen that I test my function in "interactive mode", directly running the code chunk within the test in the global environment, e.g. in my example I just run:
```R
test_dir <- withr::local_tempdir()
withr::local_dir(test_dir)
my_fun()
expect_true(file.exists("data.RData"))
```
instead of running `test_that(...)`.

In that case, I am moved to the local temp dir (and same if I use `local_options()`, the "local options" are set in the global environment) and I do not know how to undo this except manually (which is not convenient, e.g. if I setup numerous local options) or by exiting my current R session (even less convenient).

Thanks

title: Issues with handlers attribute
description:
Using `defer()` in the execution env causes a self-reference that may cause undefined behaviour (may just need a documentation note to recommend deferring expressions in private environments):

```r
local({
  withr::defer(NULL)
  print(environment())
})
#> *infloop*
```

`local_` functions cause side effects in arbitrary environments:

```r
local(envir = asNamespace("rlang"), {
  withr::local_options(list())
})

names(attributes(asNamespace("rlang")))
#> [1] "handlers"
```

Deferring expressions in a non-top-level global frame causes the message about deferred events to be printed, even though the on-exit expressions are correctly unwound.

```r
options(foo = FALSE)

local(envir = globalenv(), {
  withr::local_options(list(foo = TRUE))
})
#> Setting deferred event(s) on global environment.
#>   * Execute (and clear) with `deferred_run()`.
#>   * Clear (without executing) with `deferred_clear()`.

getOption("foo")
#> [1] FALSE
```

The handler attributes lingers around despite the handler having been called:

```r
attr(globalenv(), "handler")
#> [[1]]
#> [[1]]$expr
#> reset_options(old)
#>
#> [[1]]$envir
#> <environment: 0x7fc2d2fa98c0>
```

I would expect no message in this case and the handler attribute to be cleaned up after execution. A non-top-level global frame can be detected with:

```r
is_global_frame <- sys.parents() == 0

# TRUE if top-level
sum(is_global_frame) == 1
```

title: on.exit calls
description:
This might seem nitpicking in R, but I think it is important to learn good practice in general. Whenever you write things like

``` r
restore <- change_something()
on.exit(restore_something(restore), add = TRUE)
...
```

you introduce a potential error. If the code is interrupted after `change_something`, but before `on.exit`, then `restore_something` will never happen. 

Here is an example from devtools:
https://github.com/hadley/devtools/blob/c2ad0729e56990b5c66a4e1ef50f3aaa2b8b9c5a/R/with.r#L36-L41

This is of course everywhere, in base R and CRAN packages, not just in devtools. I think in most cases you can just do something like:

``` r
on.exit(try(restore_something(restore)), add = TRUE)
restore <- change_something()
...
```

i.e. just switch the order of the two expressions, and add a `try()`, in case there is an interruption after `on.exit()`, but before `change_something()`.

The [`targets`](https://docs.ropensci.org/targets/) package needs to call `with_seed()` a lot, and noticeable time is spent getting the R version and RNG kind. Would it be feasible to cache these in `withr` for the current R session? `digest` has a similar way of caching the platform type in a local package environment: https://github.com/eddelbuettel/digest/pull/138.

To demonstrate the bottlenecks I see in `with_seed()`:

```r
proffer::pprof(replicate(10000, withr::with_seed(0, 1)))
```

title: with_makevars() does not keep contents of existing ~/.R/Makevars
description:
When I use `with_makevars()` in the presence of an existing ~/.R/Makevars file, the contents of the latter is simply ignored.

```r
> readLines("~/.R/Makevars")
[1] "CC=/usr/local/bin/gcc"

> with_makevars(c(FC="/usr/local/bin/gfortran"), readLines(Sys.getenv("R_MAKEVARS_USER")))
[1] "FC=/usr/local/bin/gfortran"
```

The source of this issue is the delayed evaluation of the `path = makevars_user()` default argument. `makevars_user()` is only evaluated in `set_makevars()`, where the environment variable `R_MAKEVARS_USER` has already been changed to point to a temporary filename. If I pass the filename explicitly, the contents of Makevars are correctly retained.

```r
> with_makevars(c(FC="/usr/local/bin/gfortran"), readLines(Sys.getenv("R_MAKEVARS_USER")), path="~/.R/Makevars")
[1] "CC=/usr/local/bin/gcc"      "FC=/usr/local/bin/gfortran"
```

So this issue can be fixed by forcing the evaluation of the `path` argument before passing it to `set_makevars()`.

This issue affects `local_makevars()` too.

title: Allow setting rng `kind`, `normal.kind` and `sample.kind` for `withr::with_seed`
description:
`withr::with_seed()` currently gives no easy way to force a specific RNG to be used and thus ensure true reproducibility.

This bites you if e.g. parllelising code using the `future` package, which switches to a parallel-safe L'Ecuyer-CMRG instead of the default Mersenne-Twister.

Here is a single-session reprex:

``` r
withr::with_seed(1, runif(10))
#>  [1] 0.26550866 0.37212390 0.57285336 0.90820779 0.20168193 0.89838968
#>  [7] 0.94467527 0.66079779 0.62911404 0.06178627
RNGkind("L'Ecuyer-CMRG")
withr::with_seed(1, runif(10))
#>  [1] 0.6775328 0.4273457 0.9103805 0.9557282 0.8406586 0.3436612 0.3565767
#>  [8] 0.4283901 0.4474990 0.4025935
RNGkind("default")
withr::with_seed(1, runif(10))
#>  [1] 0.26550866 0.37212390 0.57285336 0.90820779 0.20168193 0.89838968
#>  [7] 0.94467527 0.66079779 0.62911404 0.06178627
```

<sup>Created on 2021-03-11 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v1.0.0)</sup>

Quoting `?Random`:
>  If you want to reproduce work later, call set.seed (preferably with explicit values for kind and normal.kind) rather than set .Random.seed.

title: With R-devel, `with_timezone()` will need to check for a locked binding
description:
With this commit https://github.com/wch/r-source/commit/71ba5d063f97bff3ef3f12e43b5444964e6e8b26, `.sys.timezone` becomes a locked binding that will need to be unlocked by withr in order to be changed. The locked state should be restored on exit.

This R-devel change results in CRAN failures of the form:

```r
    > x <- as.Date("2019-01-01")
    >
    > # `as.POSIXct()` will always treat Date as UTC, but will show the result
    > # of the conversion in your system time zone, which can be somewhat confusing
    > if (rlang::is_installed("withr")) {
    + withr::with_timezone("UTC", print(as.POSIXct(x)))
    + withr::with_timezone("Europe/Paris", print(as.POSIXct(x)))
    + withr::with_timezone("America/New_York", print(as.POSIXct(x)))
    + }
    Error in assign(".sys.timezone", NA, envir = baseenv()) :
     cannot change value of locked binding for '.sys.timezone'
    Calls: <Anonymous> -> assign
    Error in assign(".sys.timezone", old, envir = baseenv()) :
     cannot change value of locked binding for '.sys.timezone'
    Calls: <Anonymous> -> assign
```

title: Should we have a local_temp_dir?
description:
I find this convenient in test cases:

```r
local_temp_dir <- function(pattern = "file", tmpdir = tempdir(),
                           fileext = "", envir = parent.frame()) {
  path <- tempfile(pattern = pattern, tmpdir = tmpdir, fileext = fileext)
  dir.create(path)
  setwd(path)
  do.call(
   withr::defer,
    list(
      bquote(unlink(.(path), recursive = TRUE)),
      envir = envir
    )
  )
  invisible(path)
}
```

Then the test case is just 

```r
test_that("...", {
  local_temp_dir()
  ...
})
```

title: Defer silently swallows errors?
Directories that delete themselves
description:
Currently `local_file` cannot delete directories, since by default `recursive = FALSE` for `unlink`. Here are some options.

1. Add ellipsis to `local_file` and `with_file`. This seems minimally redundant, but the function name could be confusing. In Unix, a directory is just a special type of file, right? ;-)
```r
local_file <- function(file, ..., .local_envir = parent.frame()) {
  file_nms <- names2(file)
  unnamed <- file_nms == ""
  file_nms[unnamed] <- as.character(file[unnamed])
  defer(unlink(file_nms, ...), envir = .local_envir)
  invisible(file)
}
```

2. @hadley suggested a `local_directory` function, which could be identical to the one above, or could be the following.
```r
local_link <- function(file, ..., .local_envir = parent.frame()) {
  file_nms <- names2(file)
  unnamed <- file_nms == ""
  file_nms[unnamed] <- as.character(file[unnamed])
  defer(unlink(file_nms, ...), envir = .local_envir)
  invisible(file)
}

local_file <- function(file, .local_envir = parent.frame()) {
  local_link(file, .local_envir = .local_envir)
}

local_directory <- function(directory, .local_envir = parent.frame()) {
  local_link(directory, recursive = TRUE, .local_envir = .local_envir)
}
```

If adding a function `local_directory`, it may be a good idea to deprecate the name `local_dir` in favor of `local_wd`. Thoughts?

title: Destructor syntax
withr::with_libpaths() and the peculiarities of utils::install.packages()
description:
This turns out to be (mostly) not a {withr} bug.  I'm posting what I've discovered through an unfortunate amount of troubleshooting in hopes it will help someone else.  

---
"Offending" Code:
```
a <- file.path(tempdir(), "temp")
dir.create(a)
withr::with_libpaths(a,
install.packages("purrr",
                 dependencies = "Imports")
                 )
list.dirs(a, recursive = FALSE)
```
#### Expected (Wanted) Outcome: 
{purrr} and its dependencies ({rlang}, {magrittr}) to be installed into `tempdir/temp`

#### Actual Outcome:
If {rlang}/{magrittr} are found in any directory within `.libPaths()`, they will not be installed in  `file.path(tempdir(), "temp")`; although {purrr} will be. 

The real problem is that I was getting seemingly different behavior on Windows vs Mac. On my Windows machines my external packages were installed to a different folder than either `.Library.site or .Library`. However, on my Mac they were installed to `.Library.site or .Library`.
This made it impossible to create a new package directory on my Mac that contained both a package **and** its dependencies (if the dependencies were already installed on that machine)

**Potential {withr} bug**: `withr::with_libpaths` doesn't create a pristine `.libPaths()`, even with `action = "replace`. This is because `.libPaths(new)` will still append `.Library.site, .Library` if they exist. AFAIK this is not changeable from within an R session and therefore I'm not sure there should be an `action = "replace"` option (or would require something like github.com/r-lib/callr)

---
#### It seems to start with `utils::install.packages()`:

It turns out that `install.packages` only respects `install.packages(lib=)` for the specified package (in this case {purrr}) and will ignore any dependencies ({magrittr}, {rlang}) if they are found in any of the directories in `.libPaths()`. This is IMO a really unfortunate quirk in R's {utils::install.packages()} for my case and those like here https://github.com/conda-forge/r-base-feedstock/issues/37, when people are trying to create isolated/standalone R compute environments.

#### The root of the "problem":
This behavior seems to be caused by the appending of .libPaths() *only during install of dependencies*:

https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/d6c208e464d20adc6ce080ecfaaab4ccf3f06271/src/library/utils/R/packages2.R#L84-L88

with_tempfile
description:
This takes an idea from `bquote()` and allows you to specify what variable to assign the temporary filename to in your code by surrounding it in a `.()` call. Then these files are cleaned up afterwards. The function definition and example usage is below. An alternative interface would be to have a separate argument to specify variable names to use, but I think it is a little nicer to specify them inline. Any thoughts @krlmlr?

``` r
with_tempfile <- function(code, envir = parent.frame()) {
  # Adapted from bquote
  vars <- character()
  unquote <- function(e) {
    if (is.pairlist(e))
      as.pairlist(lapply(e, unquote))
    else if (length(e) <= 1) e
    else if (e[[1]] == as.name(".")) {
      vars <<- append(vars, as.character(e[[2]]))
      e[[2]]
    }
    else as.call(lapply(e, unquote))
  }
  code <- unquote(substitute(code))
  if (length(vars) == 0) {
    stop("Must specify a variable to store the temp filename using .() in your
         code", call. = FALSE)
  }

  env <- new.env(parent = envir)
  for (var in vars) {
    assign(var, tempfile(), envir = env)
  }
  on.exit(unlink(mget(vars, envir = env)))

  eval(code, envir = env)
}

with_tempfile({
  writeLines("hi", con = .(tmp))
  writeLines("ho", con = .(tmp2))
  print(readLines(tmp))
  print(readLines(tmp2))
  files <<- append(files, tmp)
  files <<- append(files, tmp2)
```

title: 'defer' + 'scoped' side effects
description:
The goal is to enable writing, instead of this,

``` R
with_dir(directory, {
    // code
})
```

to write this:

``` R
scoped_dir(directory)
// code
```

This can be accomplished with a couple tools. The main trick is to use `on.exit`, but attach its execution to an arbitrary parent frame. We create a function `defer` that accomplishes that:

``` R
defer <- function(expr, envir = parent.frame()) {

  # Create a call that must be evaluated in the parent frame (as
  # that's where functions and symbols need to be resolved)
  call <- substitute(
    evalq(expr, envir = envir),
    list(expr = substitute(expr), envir = parent.frame())
  )

  # Use 'do.call' with 'on.exit' to attach the evaluation to
  # the exit handlers of the selected frame
  do.call("on.exit", list(substitute(call), add = TRUE), envir = envir)

  # TODO: Not sure what we should actually return.
}
```

And then create functions that provide their 'state' and 'reset' at the exit of that scope:

``` R
scoped_dir <- function(directory) {
    owd <- setwd(directory)
    defer(setwd(owd), parent.frame())
}
```

Any thoughts on whether something like this would be appropriate for `withr`?

---

For completeness, this was inspired by the discussion here: https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-devel/2013-November/067874.html

While much of the code in this package was originally derived from code in devtools it has been fairly substantially reworked by @krlmlr and I.  I think we should definitely keep Hadley and Winston as authors and attribute the original source of the code to devtools, however I am not sure if RStudio should still be listed as the copyright holder as neither Kirill or I is associated with them.

If it is decided that RStudio _should_ remain the copyright holder that is fine with me, but I wanted to get some input before we submit withr to CRAN.

Regardless we should add tests for them!
